title: the Sri Yantra
hook: a dot at the center, and two answers about who walks all the way in
tomorrow: a pinch of red powder, and she starts at the edge. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Sri Yantra's woven heart: four triangles of Shiva and five of Shakti, too tightly woven to pull apart. Today, the very center.

Some things get handed down in person or not at all: a recipe nobody writes down, a family song only the elders start, a move on the court a coach shows you once you're ready. At the very center of the Sri Yantra sits a dot no bigger than the tip of a pen. People who love this yantra give two different answers to yesterday's question, who gets to walk all the way in. Let both of them speak.
screen: `HANDED DOWN IN PERSON.` → `A DOT AT THE CENTER.` → `WHO WALKS ALL THE WAY IN?`

segments.voice: That dot is the bindu, a drop or a point. Every line so far has been leading here. Lalita's thousand names include one that calls her the one seated in the bindu. The gates, the lotuses, the woven triangles are rooms of a house; the bindu is where she's at home. A point has no size at all, and yet the whole yantra gathers to it. So, who walks in? First voice: in Sri Vidya lineages, the full worship of the yantra and its mantra are received from a teacher, through initiation, called diksha. The best case for it: the road to the center passes through every layer in order, and someone who has walked it can walk you through. A practice this deep deserves a guide, not a shortcut. Second voice: in other homes, people keep a Sri Yantra on the shelf, offer it flowers and recite her names, with no initiation at all. The best case for it: the gates face every direction, and a mother's house isn't locked to her children. Love can start at the edge and grow. Notice what each one protects. The first protects the depth of the practice. The second protects the welcome. Both voices belong to people who love the same small dot.
screen: `THE BINDU: WHERE SHE SITS.` · `ONE VOICE: THROUGH A TEACHER.` · `ONE VOICE: THE GATES ARE OPEN.` · `ONE GUARDS DEPTH; ONE, WELCOME.` · then, large: `A WHOLE HOUSE GATHERED TO ONE POINT.`

segments.voice: Make a small dot on a piece of paper, or pick one point in front of you, a mark on the wall or the head of a nail. Let your gaze rest on it, and let everything around it go soft and blurry. Each time the eyes wander, come back to the one point.
The Sri Yantra's center: the bindu, a point with no size, where the Goddess is said to sit and where every line ends.
Your line: the Sri Yantra, a whole house of lines gathered to one small point. Until tomorrow.

notes: Sri Yantra run. Confirm the name Baindavasana in the Lalita Sahasranama.

DEBATE (two views within Hinduism): Sri Vidya lineages that give the full yantra worship and mantra through diksha, versus household devotion that keeps a yantra and recites the Lalita Sahasranama without initiation. Both steelmanned; neither ranked; 'a mother's house isn't locked to her children' is offered as the open voice's case, not as doctrine. A Sri Vidya teacher should confirm the description of initiation is fair and that nothing here invites anyone to attempt the initiated rite.
